title: LEAP shape definition
description: Meta-schema for per-part shapes.json files. A shapes.json declares the TYPES and FUNCTIONS a LEAP part owns, in a language-neutral vocabulary. Per-target mapping files (parts/targets/<target>/mapping.md) describe how each construct is emitted in that target language.

owner.description: Part that owns these shapes (for cross-part reference resolution).

imports.description: Map of imported type names -> owning part path. Resolves cross-leaf type refs.

types.description: Types owned by this part. Key = type name.

methods.description: Method groups attached to types (usually types owned here). Key = type name; value = array of fn defs.

constructors.description: Constructor groups attached to opaque types. Key = type name; value = array of fn defs that return an instance of that type. Needed because opaque types hide representation — external callers cannot initialize fields, so the constructor surface must be declared.

functions.description: Free functions owned by this part. Key = function name.

OpaqueDef.description: Distinct nominal type with a hidden representation. Callers must not introspect.

representation.description: Hint for the target mapping; callers still treat the type as opaque.

fields.description: Map of field name -> FieldSpec. A FieldSpec is either a bare TypeRef (unconditional field) or an object with an optional 'when' discriminator gate. The latter lets the record express layouts where a field's presence depends on the value of a prior (sibling) field — e.g. SQLite's 'right_child' pointer that only exists on interior B-tree pages.

oneOf.description: Conditional field — present iff the 'when' predicate holds on an earlier field's value. Earlier = lexically prior in the same record's fields map. Each target emits this as an Option/nullable wrapper plus a decode-time predicate.

when.description: Gate predicate. Currently supports equality on a sibling field's value ('eq') and membership in a set ('in').

field.description: Name of the sibling field whose value gates presence.

eq.description: Field present iff sibling equals this value.

in.description: Field present iff sibling value ∈ this list.

VariantDef.description: Tagged union. Each case may have zero or more named fields. No-field cases emit as unit variants in the target.

name.description: Function/method/constructor name. Required when the FnDef appears inside a list (methods, constructors); optional when the FnDef is the value of a keyed map entry (functions).

receiver.description: For methods: how the receiver (first implicit arg) is taken. 'borrow' = immutable self, 'mut' = mutable self. Omit for free functions and constructors.

ComposeDef.description: Cross-part tagged union. Each case wraps a single imported type (declared in shapes.json.imports). Used to express a flat union (e.g. Opcode = OpcodeCore | OpcodeAgg | ...) where the inner variants live in sibling parts. Unlike 'variant', a compose case is ALWAYS a 1-field wrap around an imported type — the goal is composition, not a new algebra.

cases.description: Key = case tag (emitted as the variant discriminator in the target). Value.of = imported type the case wraps; must appear in shapes.json.imports.

oneOf.description: Named type reference. Primitive scalars: bool i8 i16 i32 i64 u8 u16 u32 u64 f32 f64 str bytes string blob unit PC. Primitive big-endian integers (for on-disk file-format decoding): u16_be u24_be u32_be u48_be u64_be i8_be i16_be i24_be i32_be i48_be i64_be f64_be — each target maps these to a byte-to-int decoder. Self-describing: varint_be (SQLite's 1-9 byte big-endian huffman varint for rowids and record headers). Otherwise resolves to a user-defined type by name (this file or via imports).

fn.description: Function / callback type. Expresses a first-class function value — e.g. a RowSink invoked by the VDBE each time a program emits a row. Each target maps this to its native callable (Rust fn ptr, C function pointer, Go func, Python callable, Zig *const fn).

list_sized_by.description: Homogeneous list of `elem` whose length is bound by a sibling field (`length_field`) in the enclosing record. Used for on-disk arrays sized by a prior count field — e.g. SQLite's cell-pointer array (cell_count × u16_be). The schema cannot verify the sibling exists and is an integer; targets check at emission time.

length_field.description: Name of the sibling field inside the enclosing record that holds the length.

codec.description: Format-specific decoder. When a format's framing doesn't map cleanly onto the shape grammar — e.g. SQLite's serial-type tagged sequence where the discriminator byte encodes both the type AND the length — declare a named codec here and let each target's mapping.md supply the concrete decoder function. The schema is intentionally opaque; all semantics live in per-target prose.

name.description: Codec identifier, e.g. 'SqliteSerialTypeSequence'. Targets dispatch on this name.

decodes.description: The conceptual output type the codec produces (usually a list<Value> or a record).
